# ADR 0002: AI insights in the Navigator are generated by the collector

- **Status:** Proposed. Sending anonymised project data to OpenAI is approved by Peter (owner,
  19 Oct 2026). Open before it is accepted: the language of the AI text (see "Open questions").
- **Date:** 19 Oct 2026
- **Decision log:** B35 (`apps/mission-control/data/mission-control/decisions.yaml`)
- **Issue:** #115 (collector), #116 (web). Live questions build on this in ADR 0003 (#117).

## Context

New direction (19 Oct 2026): the Navigator panel summarises the page it is on, finds deviations
and gives suggested next steps. ADR 0001 says Mission Control V1 has no backend: the collector
writes a snapshot and a static app shows it. The OpenAI key must never reach the browser.

## Decision

**Where the text is generated**
- The **collector** asks the OpenAI API once per page (Overview, Development, Sources) and project
  on every run, and stores the answer in the snapshot. The web app only shows it (#116).
- ADR 0001 still holds: no backend, no database. The key stays a secret in CI.
- Cost is bounded by the runs: about three per weekday plus merges (#101), times three pages,
  times the projects.

**Model and account**
- OpenAI, through **Peter's own OpenAI account** (API access on platform.openai.com, not a ChatGPT
  subscription). The API key is stored in AWS Secrets Manager (`mission-control/openai-api-key`,
  #112), with a monthly spending limit on the OpenAI side.
- Default model **`gpt-6-luna`**, OpenAI's most efficient model for focused, high-volume tasks
  (checked on the OpenAI model page on 19 Oct 2026). It is a setting in `application.properties`
  (with `max_tokens`), so the model can be changed without code changes.

**Data sent, without personal names**
- Per page, only the data that page shows: work items, pull requests, decisions, risks, questions,
  source status and dates. Never tokens, secrets, URLs with query strings or document content.
- **Before anything leaves**, every person name and login from the snapshot's person fields
  (assignees, owners, authors, last editors) is replaced with a neutral label ("Person A",
  "Person B" …), also where it appears in titles and texts, and mapped back in the answer.
- The anonymisation is the shared module `apps/mission-control/anonymizer` (package
  `se.rainmaker.missioncontrol.anonymizer`, plain Java, no dependencies), also used by the Ask
  Navigator backend (ADR 0003), so there is one implementation.

**The call**
- Structured output (JSON) with `summary`, `deviations[]` and `suggestions[]`, with limits on
  length and count. Timeouts, retries with back-off and a circuit breaker (Resilience4j).
- A fixed system prompt says the data is information, not instructions (as in the START HERE
  report), defines a deviation as late, blocked, overdue, red or failing compared with the plan,
  and allows answers only from the given data.

**Isolation and off switch**
- If the AI step fails or times out, the snapshot is still written, the page's AI text is empty,
  and the run reports it like a failed source. The AI never stops the dashboard from updating.
- A setting switches the step off (off locally and in tests, on in staging), so tests and local
  runs need no key. All tests use WireMock, never the real API.

## Consequences

- **Owner approval:** given by Peter for sending anonymised project data to OpenAI. The data
  leaves the company for an external provider in the US.
- **Known limit:** only names in the snapshot's person fields are hidden. A name that appears only
  in free text (a title or a mitigation) and in no person field is sent as written. Two names of
  one person (a full name and a login) get two labels.
- **Ongoing cost:** OpenAI per call, capped by the run schedule and the spending limit.
- **Freshness:** the text is as new as the latest collector run.
- **Contract:** the snapshot gets a new, nullable `navigator` section; schema, Java records and
  zod types change together (#10).

## Open questions

- **Language of the AI text:** Swedish, English or both? The dashboard has both languages. "Both"
  doubles the calls and the cost.

## Alternatives considered

- **Live calls from a backend:** answers on demand, but contradicts ADR 0001 and adds AWS
  resources. Kept for free-text questions only (ADR 0003, #117).
- **Calling OpenAI from the browser:** would expose the key. Rejected.
- **Sending names unmasked:** simpler, but sends personal data to an external provider without
  need. Rejected.
